subject: how to read status (checked="checked" or not) of custom checkbox?

messages.author: 8a98edc55c6202fc
messages.subject: how to read status (checked="checked" or not) of custom checkbox?
parts:
I have created a table that includes a checkbox and is displayed with dataTableOutput.
I use two selectInputs to selected some checkboxes in the table. I simply re-generate the table but adding checked="checked" to the rows I want to select.

The problem is that  input$row is not updated. It is only updated if I click on a checkbox to select it. Then all the rows including then ones set by checked="checked" is returned by input$row. How do I make shiny catch the selected rows? Or is there a better way to check the checkboxes?




output$MANAGE_data <- renderDataTable({
  
  # Select rows
  checked=rep('',nrow(users_data()))
  if(!(input$MANAGE_filter_by=="") & !is.null(input$MANAGE_filter_select)){
    if(!(input$MANAGE_filter_select=="")){
      checked[        users_data()[[input$MANAGE_filter_by]] == input$MANAGE_filter_select    ]   ='checked="checked"'
    }
  }
  
  
  
  # Add checkbox column
  addCheckBoxes <- paste0('<input type="checkbox" ',' id=' ,'row',1:nrow(users_data()),' ',checked,' name="row" value="', 1:nrow(users_data()), '">')
  cbind.data.frame(Select=addCheckBoxes,users_data()           ,stringsAsFactors = F)
  
  

}
                                      
                                      
                                      ,options=list(iDisplayLength = 15,aoColumnDefs=manage_table_settings(), aoColumns=NULL,bAutoWidth=FALSE    )
)

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: how to read status (checked="checked" or not) of custom checkbox?
parts:
It seems you want to mimic checkboxGroupInput() by providing raw HTML
to DataTables. That is a little hackish, but I completely understand
the motivation. Unfortunately checkboxGroupInput() is slightly more
complicated than just a series of checkboxes.

I did not test it, but I guess you can remove `name="row"` in your
checkbox, then

sapply(1:nrow(users_data()), function(i) {
isTRUE(input[[paste0("row", i)]])
})

probably gives you a vector of TRUE/FALSE, in which TRUE means that
row is selected.

Regards,
Yihui
